Analysis of variance with expected mean squares

Source: R/ems.R
vlm_ems.Rd

The analysis of variance of a linear model fitted by ordinary least squares, with the expected mean squares of each source when some effects are random, F tests built from the appropriate (synthesised) error terms with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, and the method-of-moments (Type 3) estimates of the variance components. This is SAS PROC GLM with a RANDOM statement and the TEST option (Examples 1.3.2 and 2.5.3.1 of the book).

Usage

vlm_ems(fixed, data, random = NULL, type = 3, class = NULL)

# Default S3 method
vlm_ems(fixed, data, random = NULL, type = 3, class = NULL)

Arguments

fixed

two-sided formula with every effect of the model, random effects included, in SAS MODEL order (for example PCVdif ~ drug + drug:herd + dose + dose:drug).

data

a data frame with the variables.

random

one-sided formula of the effects of fixed that are random (for example ~ drug:herd); NULL for a fixed-effects analysis.

type

type of sums of squares: 3 (default) or 1.

class

optional character vector of numeric variables to treat as classification variables.

Value

A list of class c("vlm_ems", "vlm_result", "list") with anova (source, df, sum of squares, mean square, expected mean square, F, error degrees of freedom and p-value), coefficients (the coefficients of the variance components in each expected mean square), error_terms (the combination of mean squares used as the error of each test) and components (Type 3 estimates of the variance components).

Details

The sum of squares of a source is a quadratic form \(SS = \mathbf{y}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{y}\): for Type 3, \(\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{X}\mathbf{C}\mathbf{L}^{\top}(\mathbf{L}\mathbf{C}\mathbf{L}^{\top})^{-1}\mathbf{L} \mathbf{C}\mathbf{X}^{\top}\) with \(\mathbf{C} = (\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{X})^{-1}\) in the sum-to-zero coding and \(\mathbf{L}\) selecting the columns of the source; for Type 1, the projection on the columns added by the source. With random effects \(\mathbf{u}_k \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \sigma_k^2\mathbf{I})\) of design \(\mathbf{Z}_k\), $$E(MS) = \sigma^2 + \sum_k \frac{\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{Z}_k^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{Z}_k)}{DF}\,\sigma_k^2 + Q(\mathrm{fixed}).$$ The error term of a source is the combination \(\sum_r a_r MS_r\) of mean squares of other random sources and the residual whose expectation equals that of the source under the null hypothesis; its degrees of freedom are \((\sum_r a_r MS_r)^2 / \sum_r (a_r MS_r)^2 / DF_r\) (Satterthwaite 1946). Equating the mean squares of the random sources and the error to their expectations gives the Type 3 estimates of the variance components.

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi. Section 1.3.2 and Appendix G.

Satterthwaite, F. E. (1946). An approximate distribution of estimates of variance components. Biometrics Bulletin, 2, 110-114.

See also

vlm_fit

Other VetResearchLMM models: vlm_compare(), vlm_fit(), vlm_random()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

# Example 1.3.2: PROC GLM; CLASS herd dose drug; MODEL PCVdif = drug herd(drug) dose dose*drug;
# RANDOM herd(drug) / TEST;
em <-
  vlm_ems(
      fixed  = PCVdif ~ drug + drug:herd + dose + dose:drug
    , data   = ex124
    , random = ~ drug:herd
    , type   = 3
    , class  = "herd"
    )
em
#> Type 3 analysis of variance of PCVdif
#> 
#> Analysis of variance
#>     source df     ss     ms                                         ems      F
#>       drug  1  1.722  1.722 Var(Residual) + 10 Var(drug:herd) + Q(drug) 0.3048
#>  drug:herd  2  11.30  5.650           Var(Residual) + 10 Var(drug:herd)  23.97
#>       dose  1  172.6  172.6                     Var(Residual) + Q(dose)  732.4
#>  drug:dose  1 0.1562 0.1562                Var(Residual) + Q(drug:dose) 0.6629
#>   Residual 34  8.014 0.2357                               Var(Residual)       
#>  den_df      p
#>       2  0.636
#>      34 <1e-04
#>      34 <1e-04
#>      34  0.421
#>       .      .
#> 
#> Error terms of the tests
#>     source           error
#>       drug 1 MS(drug:herd)
#>  drug:herd  1 MS(Residual)
#>       dose  1 MS(Residual)
#>  drug:dose  1 MS(Residual)
#> 
#> Type 3 estimates of the variance components
#>  component estimate
#>  drug:herd   0.5415
#>   Residual   0.2357
#> 
#> Sources: Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998); Searle, Casella and McCulloch
#> (1992); Satterthwaite (1946). Full references: vlm_cite(x).

# one observation deleted: the expected mean squares of drug and herd(drug) no longer match
# (Table 1.3.2.3)
em1 <-
  vlm_ems(
      fixed  = PCVdif ~ drug + drug:herd + dose + dose:drug
    , data   = ex124[-1, ]
    , random = ~ drug:herd
    , type   = 3
    , class  = "herd"
    )
em1$coefficients
#>           drug:herd Residual
#> drug       9.714286        1
#> drug:herd  9.722222        1
#> dose       0.000000        1
#> drug:dose  0.000000        1
#> Residual   0.000000        1
